pr_title: cmsis_rots_v1: fix for clearing signal flags in osSignalWait.
pr_body:
we use flag 0 in osSignalWait function to wait for
any single signal flag, but with this 0 flag,
it won't clear thread signal results as expected in "thread_def->signal_results &= signals".
we need to check whether signal flag is 0 firstly.

fix: #37182 

Signed-off-by: Chen Peng1 <peng1.chen@intel.com>
pr_comments: hi @dcpleung, could you help review this? thanks.

issue_context.title: cmsis_v1 osSignalWait doesn't clear the signals properly when any signal mask is set
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
cmsis_v1 osSignalWait doesn't clear the signals properly when any signal mask is set; so at the next call, the previous bits are still set even if not raised again.

**To Reproduce**
call osSignalSet(thread, 0x1)
call osSignalWait(thread, 0x0) -- special 0x0 flag to wait for any signal
check that evt.value.signals is really 0x1
call osSignalWait(thread, 0x0)
evt.value.signals is still 0x1 !

**Expected behavior**
call osSignalSet(thread, 0x1)
call osSignalWait(thread, 0x0) -- special 0x0 flag to wait for any signal
check that evt.value.signals is really 0x1
call osSignalWait(thread, 0x0)
check that evt.value.signals is really 0x0

**Impact**
Bug making the signaling of any not usable.

**Logs and console output**
NA

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
Any


**Additional context**
My patch here 
[0001-Fix-an-y-signal-mask-bug.patch.gz](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/6872080/0001-Fix-an-y-signal-mask-bug.patch.gz)

review_comments: Is it better to define a macro for "0"?
I think we don't need to define an external macro for 0, it's not a common flag, it's just used to clear the signal flags by setting its value as 0.
